title: AFTER-ACTION REPORT ARM42 — Dugruk Ork Attack on FOB Ember
meta: LOG REF: CGN-ARM-0042 · FILED BY: CPT Brenticles · CLEARANCE: Command Eyes Only
body:
After-Action Report: FOB Ember

Orks Inside the FOB

The Ork counterattack came as a shock but not total suprise. The bulk of 1st Battalion was committed to frontline action beyond immediate response of the FOB. 7th Company: a squad of the Hotshots, the command element, and two squadrons of Calinosian Hazechargers screening the perimeter, under the acting authority of Platoon Commander Ansel Draeth. Against them came Warboss Dugruk and the hard core of his warband — some survivors of OP Swift Ash, returning for what they'd lost. Orks were found to be already within the perimeter by the time a Hazecharger squadron was able to rush into the action.

Hazechargers Routed

Supported by fire from Hotshots holding the main building, the Hazechargers attempted to secure the main building before the orks could reach it but imediate heavy casualties. Before they could respond and counter the enemy they suffered heavy losses becoming combat ineffective and fell back.

With the perimeter broken, LT Draeth made the call every gaurdsmen dreads: withdraw. Consolidate what remained. Live to hold the next line instead of dying on this one.

The order went out. The Hotshots did not follow it.

Kellen's Last Stand

Lt Kellen Voss and his nine Hotshots held position atop the main structure as the withdrawal order came through, and stayed. Whether it was Voss's call alone or the squad's to a man, I cannot say with certainty — only that they did their duty to the emperor and Calinosian name.

They gave no ground even as the Ork's climbed atop the FOB's central structure for a direct charge. The Hotshots held that high ground last in the compound. What followed was close, brutal, and without mercy carnage on either side — hellpistols and combat blades against choppas and sheer weight of numbers, fought at arm's length in the ash and smoke until there was not one member of Voss' squad left.

Every Hotshot who stayed atop that structure died that day. But they did not die quickly, and they did not die in vain — Dugruk's warband paid in blood and, more importantly, time. For every minute of that rooftop held, time the withdrawing elements used to disengage and the reinforcements needed to close the distance.

Pyrrhic Victory

FOB Ember fell. It did not fall fast, or easily. I record the outcome as a strategic success purchased at severe cost — the delay bought by LT Voss and his Hotshots, layered atop the price already paid by the Hazechargers, denied Dugruk the clean victory he came for and gave 1st Battalion the window it needed to respond.

I am recommeding LT Voss and the other Hotshots posthumously be awarded the Maltese Medallion for their actions. As well as unit citations for 7th Company, 1st Hotshots and 1st and 2nd Calvary Squadrons.

Personal Note

There is talk over the Vox that Theater command witnessed the battle remotely and seem to think us Calinosians are fighters that bring the hell of our planet with us. Some have called us Hellfighters.

Though incorrect, it seems to be catching among the other regiments. I'm choosing to not correct the record. Only that I hope we continue to live up to the name.

title: FOB EMBER TO 407TH COMMAND
body:
[LT Vorne] Vorne to Command, contact report. Visual on hostile Ork force approaching. Platoon sized element with light support. Requesting instructions.
[CPT Brenticles] Vorne, this is Captain Brenticles. Hold FOB Ember through all hell. Reinforcements will be enroute direct.
[LT Vorne] We'll show them the meaning.

title: Entry — Third night in the ash fields
meta: LOG REF: CGN-SJ-0091 · FILED BY: Unattributed, recovered from field kit · CLEARANCE: Chaplaincy Review
body: The fog doesn't lift out here. We've stopped waiting for it to. Command says that's the point — we're the ones who see through it, or near enough. I believe them most days.

title: To the family of a Shock Trooper, 2nd Line
meta: LOG REF: CGN-LL-0091 · FILED BY: Regimental Chaplaincy, with Casualty Roll CGN-CR-0104 · CLEARANCE: Next of Kin
body: Tell them I made it further than I thought I would, and that the company held the line because of people like the ones standing next to me — not because of anything I did alone.

title: AFTER-ACTION REPORT ARM41 — OP SWIFT ASH: RELIEF OF FOB EMBER
meta: LOG REF: CGN-ARM-0041 · FILED BY: CPT Brenticles · CLEARANCE: Command Eyes Only
body:
Mission Objective

Rapid insertion and extraction of Blood Angels Captain from FOB Ember, Volcanus Theater near Hive Deathmire.

Engagement Summary

Company 7 inserted at best speed through ash-fall and hostile fire. The Captain was found heavily pressed, Ork forces had closed on the FOB perimeter and were moving to overwhelm the position. I assessed the break-in point and committed the Hotshot squad for immediate rapid insertion.

The Hotshots dove straight into the FOB interior and made hard contact with the Captain. They locked into the scrum with him as Orks pressed in from all sides — the three who fell did so holding the line beside him, their lasguns bright in the ash-choked air, buying time with their bodies for the larger plan to turn.

While Hotshots and the Blood Angel held the center, Calinosian troopers took the flank position on the tower works and established plunging fire from above, pouring concentrated fire down into the Ork mass. The two Hippogriffs concentrated their fire on the FOB perimeter itself — the Rogal Dorn's heavy rounds tore through the encirclement while the Centaur APC laid covering fire across the kill zone.

The Orks, hammered from above and from the flanks, their assault broken by the weight of coordinated fire, fell back. The perimeter held.

Outcome

The Blood Angel was retrieved alive. Condition: severely wounded but ambulatory. The momentum of the breakthrough was immediately leveraged into a coordinated counterattack against Ork heavy elements that had massed for the encirclement. Results of that secondary phase are pending full assessment, but initial reports indicate significant enemy losses.

Commander's Note

This was the 4th's first combat action since activation. Company 7 conducted a textbook rescue-under-fire insertion, with Hotshots hitting the center of the storm while supporting elements pinned and broke the enemy assault. The three hotshots who fell did so holding the line beside an Astartes, their names entered into the rolls.

The Blood Angels Captain survived in critical condition. He will live to fight again.
